# Command line

Every flag `nish --help` lists, in the order and the groups it lists them. [The CLI](../guide/using-nish/cli.md) in the guide shows them at work; the [diagnostic index](diagnostics.md) lists every code a check can report.

## Usage

```text
nish <file.ts> [more.ts ...] [flags]   compile to LLVM IR
nish run [flags] <file.ts> [args ...]  build, cache and run it
nish run --watch <file.ts> [args ...]  rebuild and rerun it on each edit
nish upgrade [<version>] [--check]     install a newer release
nish -v, --version | -h, --help
```

## Build

<scalar-field name="-o, --output" type="&lt;file.ll&gt;|&lt;dir&gt;/">

where the IR goes; a dir gets one per module

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="--link" type="&lt;exe&gt;">

link a native binary; the entry exports main

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="--profile" type="speed|size|debug|wasi">

the link recipe; speed is -O3 with LTO

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="--cpu" type="x86-64-v3">

allow AVX2; such a binary needs it to start

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="--target" type="&lt;triple&gt;|host">

stamp the IR with a target's data layout

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="-g">

DWARF debug info, for gdb and lldb

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="--threads">

an arena per thread, for --emit-napi-async

</scalar-field>

## Check

<scalar-field name="--fix">

apply the safe fixes in place, then recheck

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="--json">

each diagnostic as one JSON line on stdout

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="--warn-portability">

warn where TypeScript would answer otherwise

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="--no-warn-performance">

silence the performance warnings

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="--deny-panics">

refuse an unproven panic in your package

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="--deny-retention">

refuse retained arena memory in your package

</scalar-field>

## Capabilities

<scalar-field name="--capabilities">

print what the program can reach, on stderr

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="--allow" type="&lt;cap&gt;[,&lt;cap&gt;...]">

refuse a program that reaches more

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="--deny" type="&lt;cap&gt;[,&lt;cap&gt;...]">

refuse a program that reaches these

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="--deterministic">

same float bits everywhere, no clock or I/O

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="--sandbox[=best-effort]">

confine a Linux binary to what main reaches

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="--emit-capabilities" type="&lt;file.json&gt;">

write the capability report

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="--update-capability-lock">

record what each dependency reaches

</scalar-field>

## Interop

<scalar-field name="--emit-header" type="&lt;file.h&gt;">

a C header for the exports

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="--emit-dts" type="&lt;file.d.ts&gt;">

their typings, and a &lt;file>.mjs loader

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="--host" type="&lt;file.ts&gt;">

a page module whose functions wasm imports

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="--emit-napi" type="&lt;shim.c&gt;">

a Node-API shim, to load them from Node

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="--emit-napi-async" type="&lt;shim.c&gt;">

the same, plus a promise for each export

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="--emit-ts" type="&lt;dir&gt;">

the program as TypeScript, instead of IR

</scalar-field>

## Inspect

<scalar-field name="--emit-ast">

print the parse tree, one line per node

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="--emit-checked">

print what the checker recorded

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="--emit-panics" type="&lt;file.json&gt;">

list every place the program can panic

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="--emit-arena" type="&lt;file.json&gt;">

write the arena retention report

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="--explain-memory">

why loops and functions keep their memory

</scalar-field>

## Code generation

<scalar-field name="--number-mode" type="i32|f64">

what a bare number is; i32 by default

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="--compat">

compatibility dialect; accepts nothing yet

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="--plain">

the IR without LLVM's attributes

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="--no-strict-exports">

keep every function externally visible

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="--no-stack-alloc">

keep every value off the stack

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="--runtime-decls">

declare the runtime even when unused

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="--json">

diagnostics as JSON lines, fixes included

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="--fix">

apply those fixes; read only what is left

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="nish run &lt;file.ts&gt;">

</scalar-field>

## Exit codes

```text
0 ok, 1 rejected, 2 usage, 3 toolchain, 70 a compiler bug: report it
```

What each one means is the guide's [exit codes](../guide/using-nish/cli.md#exit-codes) table.

## Examples

```sh
nish run hello.ts       # build, cache and run a program
nish app.ts --link app  # write app.ll and a binary, app
nish --fix src/*.ts     # rewrite what the compiler can fix
NO_COLOR=1 nish --help  # this text, without colour
```
